claims.statement: The Asaas client is server-only, selects production only when `ASAAS_ENV` is `production` and otherwise uses sandbox, treats a missing API key as unconfigured, and aborts provider requests after 12 seconds rather than leaving checkout blocked.

Asaas payments use `pedidoId` as `externalReference`; customer lookup/creation validates CPF/CNPJ, payment creation supports PIX, boleto, and hosted credit-card billing, and PIX transfers support seller settlement.
The Asaas webhook rejects an invalid timing-safe `asaas-access-token` comparison, returns 500 without service-role configuration, and acknowledges incomplete or unsupported events as ignored.

A paid Asaas event advances an order only after its external reference resolves to an order whose stored charge ID matches `payment.id` and whose received value is at least the order amount; it then persists paid order and line-item state.

After payment persistence, Asaas processing performs buyer/seller notifications, status email, and internal/Uber routing as best-effort work, capturing notification or routing failures instead of undoing confirmed payment; cancellation-class events invoke the stock-restoration RPC and email cancellation.

Uber Direct is disabled unless customer ID, client ID, and client secret are all present; it acquires and caches a client-credentials OAuth token in process memory and uses the configured credentials rather than a different base URL to distinguish sandbox from production.

Uber Direct delivery creation quotes before creating a delivery, formats addresses as unstructured Brazilian addresses, normalizes contacts to E.164, and returns delivery ID, status, and tracking URL for persistence.

The Uber Direct callback registered at `/webhooks/uber-direct` is rewritten to `/api/webhooks/uber-direct`; with a configured signing key it requires a timing-safe HMAC-SHA256 `x-uber-signature`, but with no key the current implementation intentionally accepts the request.

Uber delivery webhooks update a route by `uber_delivery_id`, map recognized provider statuses to internal route statuses, persist tracking URL when supplied, and attempt the out-for-delivery buyer notice only after an `EmTransito` update.

Meta WhatsApp sending requires token and phone ID, normalizes numbers with Brazilian country code, posts text to Graph API v21.0, and returns false rather than pretending delivery when it is unconfigured or the number is too short.

The Meta WhatsApp webhook GET returns the challenge only for its configured verify token, while POST verifies raw-body HMAC-SHA256 with `WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET` and fails closed when the secret or signature is absent or invalid.

The WhatsApp support bot creates or finds an open conversation by normalized phone number, only enables sensitive order lookup for an identified user whose saved order contact phone matches the sender, and acknowledges without processing if service role or OpenAI is unavailable.

BubbleWhats sending is limited to `POST /send-message`, returns an explicit unconfigured or status-classified failure result, and its inbound endpoint requires a timing-safe query-string secret while only logging/observing provider events.
Resend returns an explicit unsent result without its API key, and the centralized order-status notifier catches all errors so email delivery cannot reverse an already persisted order status.

ViaCEP lookup returns null for invalid, unavailable, or provider-marked-invalid CEPs, while Google Routes is server-only and returns typed failure instead of route metrics when unconfigured, cost-limited, missing a route, or unavailable; a Google Maps direction link needs no key.
The Google Routes daily call ceiling defaults to 5000 and is maintained only in process memory, so it is a per-instance loop/cost brake rather than a durable global serverless quota.

`TURNSTILE_ATIVO` is currently `false`, so `TurnstileWidget` neither loads nor renders and `verificarTurnstile` returns true before checking its secret or token; login, registration, and checkout consequently accept requests without Turnstile verification.

Sentry is initialized for client, Node, and Edge with default PII sending disabled; absent DSN leaves it a no-op, client replay masks text and blocks media, and the Next config wires build-time source-map upload credentials and browser security headers.
The checked-in `.env.example` contains only copy instructions and documents no integration configuration variables, so deployment configuration must be maintained and verified outside that template.

The signed Asaas webhook and manual payment-verification fallback converge on `confirmarPagamentoPedido`, which treats already-paid or later order statuses as an idempotent no-op before it can notify or dispatch again.

After a paid order is persisted, internal dispatch stores null route metrics on Google Routes failure while retaining a keyless Maps link, and Uber Direct is considered only when no internal run was created and the order is otherwise eligible.

The buyer-triggered `verificarPagamento` Server Action reads only the caller's order through `pedidos_cliente`, checks the stored Asaas charge, delegates to confirmation only for `RECEIVED` or `CONFIRMED`, and permits one verification per order every 15 seconds.

Payment confirmation uses `dt_pagamento` as its idempotency marker and conditionally updates only an order whose marker is still null, so concurrent webhook and manual verification executions leave only the winning writer to update line items and run downstream effects.

Checkout persists each order before attempting its Asaas charge; it conditionally stores the charge ID and cancels a newly created charge best effort if a concurrent execution already stored one, reporting a cancellation failure as a possible ghost charge.

The WhatsApp bot validates its raw-body signature before checking service-role or bot configuration, then acknowledges without parsing or creating a conversation when either required service is unavailable.

The currently disabled Turnstile path would, when enabled with a server secret, fail closed on a missing token, rejected response, HTTP error, or network error, and sends the token and optional remote IP to Cloudflare with an eight-second timeout.

Meta Pixel is loaded only in the `/venda-no-industria` and `/armazeneconosco` layouts; it sends an initial PageView, tracks later client navigation without duplicating the initial view, and has a no-JavaScript image fallback permitted by the public-route CSP.
Google Routes and Geocoding share the same in-process daily-call counter and accept either `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` or the legacy `GOOGLE_MAPS_API`, choosing the first nonempty value.

Uber Direct callbacks acknowledge database update errors after reporting them to Sentry, but the subsequent `EmTransito` buyer notice is not caught locally and can prevent the final acknowledgement; there is no provider event-ID deduplication.
